notice: Authored synthetic context and suggestions for contract tests, not real user memory or live AI quality evidence.

context.text: I make video game review videos.

uses.title: Strengthen a review script
uses.input: Your draft, intended audience and tests you actually ran.
uses.output: Claims that exceed the observations, workflow-specific caveats and proposed wording.
uses.why_useful: For your review videos, translate hardware observations into claims you can support.
uses.try_prompt: Use these workload-fit criteria to review this script. Flag untested claims and suggest revisions.
limits: The saved lesson does not supply game benchmarks or establish game quality.

uses.title: Plan the tests your review is missing
uses.input: A product claim and the real workloads you want to discuss.
uses.output: A short list of observations needed before making each recommendation.
uses.why_useful: Know what evidence to collect before recording a verdict.
uses.try_prompt: Use my review methods to plan the missing workload tests for this video.
limits: This produces a test plan, not completed measurements.

uses.title: Develop an original sketch premise
uses.input: A mundane inconvenience and a fictional setting.
uses.output: A premise in which an excessive procedure creates the next problem.
uses.why_useful: Start from an everyday situation without copying a source scene.
uses.try_prompt: Use the saved absurd-procedure method to develop a premise about scheduling a team lunch.
limits: High-level structural technique; no claim of reproducing a specific person.

uses.title: Turn a premise into escalating beats
uses.input: Your original premise and the character's ordinary goal.
uses.output: A beat outline where each attempted solution creates a new cost.
uses.why_useful: Move from a funny setup to a scene that develops.
uses.try_prompt: Use this method to outline five escalating beats for my premise.
limits: Keep the invented rule understandable; comedic effectiveness remains subjective.

uses.title: Find where a draft loses its internal logic
uses.output: Places where escalation feels arbitrary and concrete revision suggestions.
uses.why_useful: Revise existing work instead of always asking for a new skit.
uses.try_prompt: Review this draft against the saved procedure-and-consequence criteria.
limits: A source-based critique, not a prediction of audience reaction.

uses.title: Plan a retake of a blurry portrait
uses.input: The image or an accurate description of sharp and blurred areas, plus camera settings.
uses.output: A focus-versus-motion diagnosis order and the next retake checks.
uses.why_useful: Avoid changing shutter speed when the problem is the focus plane.
uses.try_prompt: Use my portrait troubleshooting method to plan a retake from these observations.
limits: The saved lesson does not cover lighting, composition or pricing.

uses.title: Review a planned focus fix
uses.input: Your proposed camera-setting changes and observed blur.
uses.output: Which changes address the observed failure and what remains untested.
uses.why_useful: Check the reasoning before another shoot.
uses.try_prompt: Review my proposed fix against the saved focus and motion distinctions.
limits: No claim to inspect an image unless the host actually supports and receives it.
